Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

cōnsequor

cōnsequor, cōnsequī, cōnsecūtus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent; with an accusative, or ut and the subjunctive

achieve, attain, get; follow as a result, result

In this lexicon

  • achieve

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.24.3: id forīs cēnitandō facillimē cōnsequēre; Traupman 179, 321: aliquid cōnsequī, to get somewhere, to accomplish something

  • result

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.19: ex quō fit ut pudōrem rubor, terrōrem pallor et tremor cōnsequātur (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • cūrā ut valeās; id forīs cēnitandō facillimē cōnsequēre

    Look after your health; you’ll achieve that most easily by eating out a lot.Cic. Fam. 9.24.3

    In the entry for achieve

  • sēcūrī adversus hominēs, sēcūrī adversus deōs rem difficillimam adsecūtī sunt, ut illīs nē vōtō quidem opus esset

    Safe from men, safe from gods, they have achieved the hardest thing of all: they have no need even to pray for anything.Tac. Germ. 46.5–6

    In the entry for achieve

  • quam ut adipīscantur omnēs optant, eandem accūsant adeptam

    Everyone hopes to reach it, and complains of it once it is reached.Cic. Sen. 4

    In the entry for achieve
